title.narrative: Output 1.2. Increased institutional capacity of workers’ organizations

description.narrative:
1. The Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) has participated in key annual national tripartite planning foras including for the Tripartite Negotiating Forum(TNF) and the Decent Work Country Programme(DWCP) National Steering Committee meetings. The ZCTU has developed and presented proposals to influence sectoral, national and sub-regional, regional and global processes, policies and programmes:
a. A Bipartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed on by the Employers’ Confederation of Zimbabwe (EMCOZ) and Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) to advance a common agenda on building a culture of social dialogue, address the challenges related to freedom of association and protection of the right to organize, fragmentation of social security schemes, general economic and business challenges, rising poverty and inequality among others. b. The Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions prepared, adopted and presented the following proposals and positions to the Government of Zimbabwe: (i) The role of Trade Unions in supporting the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area(ACFTA) (ii) Commentary on the Labour Amendment Bill (iii) Statement on ending Violence and Harassment of women and girls and ratification of ILO Convention No. 190 on ending violence and harassment in the world of work. (iv) Commentary on the 2023 National Budget Statement (v) Inputs for the national Formalisation Strategy (vi) Inputs into the SDGs Monitoring Matrix Update for 2023. 1. The ILO through funding from ILO Regular Budget Supplementary Account(RBSA) and Regular Budgetary Technical Cooperation(RBTC) resources organised the capacity building workshops and provided technical expertise in the various work areas as part of the implementation of the Decent Work Country Programme.

Output 1.2. Increased institutional capacity of workers’ organizations

description.narrative: 1. The Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions developed a new strategic plan for 2022-2026. a. This Strategic Plan has four(4) strategic themes:(i) Sustainability and viability, (ii) Advocacy towards influencing national policy, (iii) Strengthening organisational capacity and (iv) Strengthening membership participation. b. The key results include a 10% membership growth and retention, advocacy on international labour standards and policy inputs into labour reforms and promoting gender equality- especially ratification of C189 on domestic workers, C190 on violence and harassment and C183 on maternity protection. 1. The ILO through funding from ILO Regular Budget Supplementary Account and Regular Budgetary Technical Cooperation resources organised a capacity building and orientation workshops around the ZCTU's 9th Elective Congress and provided technical expertise to the new leadership. a. The ZCTU has also received support through their participation in on-going development cooperation programmes including the the ILO/EU Spotlight Initiative and support to the follow-up on comments/observations/recommendations of ILO Supervisory Bodies.
